correctness.rationale: Reduced strict reversal forces survivor win totals \(r_{i+1}-r_i\ge1\); full strict reversal forces \(w_i-w_{i+1}\ge1\). Writing \(w_i=r_i+q_i\) yields \(q_i-q_{i+1}\ge2\), hence the deleted player participates in at least \((n-1)(n-2)\) matches. Also \(r_{n-1}\ge n-2\) and strict full scores imply \(w_i\ge2n-3-i\), whose sum gives \(3\binom{n-1}{2}\). The explicit decisive-match construction attains both bounds; the \(n=3\) load case is checked separately.
risks: Repeated meetings and unbalanced schedules are allowed, as in the source model.

evidence: Exact all-\(n\) minima for two natural scheduling costs.
value.rationale: The motivating literature treats large schedules as a realism defect. Total match count and maximum participant load are canonical sparsity measures, and the theorem gives complete sharp formulas for every \(n\), with one construction attaining both.
risks: No uniqueness classification of extremal schedules is claimed.

final_claim: For every \(n\ge3\), a win-count Borda tournament whose survivor ranking reverses completely after deleting the last-ranked player needs at least \(3\binom{n-1}{2}\) matches, sharply; the minimum possible maximum player load is \(3\) for \(n=3\) and \((n-1)(n-2)\) for \(n\ge4\).
limitations: Win-count Borda with repeated matches; no balanced-schedule constraint.
